title: Design a social news feed
prompt: Millions of users open the app and expect their personalized timeline in under 200ms, but every post from a popular account must reach all of their followers. Reads massively dominate writes, so the dominant forcing constraint is FAN-OUT under heavy read-skew: precompute each user's feed when a post is written, then serve it instantly. Draw the path from a user posting, through a feed service that fans the post out asynchronously into per-user feeds, to the cached materialized feed a reader pulls — backed by a durable store for posts and the social graph.

criteria.label: Users post and read through a client
criteria.metWhy: Good — the flow starts from the user posting and pulling their feed.
criteria.why: Add a User/Client component as the entry point for both writes (posting) and reads (loading the feed).

criteria.label: Traffic enters through a balancer or API gateway
criteria.metWhy: Nice — a front door spreads read-heavy traffic across the service tier.
criteria.why: Put a Load Balancer or API Gateway in front so the read-dominant traffic can spread across multiple service instances.

criteria.label: A feed service handles posts and feed requests
criteria.metWhy: Core compute tier present — it accepts posts and serves timelines.
criteria.why: Add a Server/Service to receive new posts, trigger fan-out, and assemble feeds for readers.

criteria.label: Fan-out happens asynchronously via a queue
criteria.metWhy: Async fan-out — a write can reach thousands of follower feeds without blocking the poster.
criteria.why: A single post may need to land in thousands of follower feeds. Add a Queue so fan-out-on-write happens asynchronously instead of in the request path.

criteria.label: Materialized feeds served from a cache
criteria.metWhy: Cache absorbs the read-skew — precomputed timelines return in milliseconds.
criteria.why: Reads dominate writes. Add a Cache to hold each user's precomputed feed so reads don't recompute or hit the database every time.

criteria.label: Posts and the social graph live in a durable store
criteria.metWhy: Durable source of truth for posts and follower relationships.
criteria.why: Add a Database to durably store posts and the social/follower graph that drives fan-out.

criteria.label: Service publishes fan-out work to the queue
criteria.metWhy: Write path enqueues fan-out work instead of doing it inline.
criteria.why: Connect the Service to the Queue so a new post is published as fan-out jobs rather than processed synchronously.

criteria.label: Read path serves feeds from the cache
criteria.metWhy: Reads hit the materialized feed cache first.
criteria.why: Connect the Service to the Cache so timeline reads pull precomputed feeds instead of rebuilding them.

criteria.label: Service persists to the durable store
criteria.metWhy: Service reads/writes posts and the graph from the database.
criteria.why: Connect the Service to the Database to persist posts and read the follower graph for fan-out and cache misses.
